answer: Use a trust-graph gate. Honest agents form dense, interlinked neighborhoods, while a sybil farm is a lonely knoll of fake accounts tied to the real network by only a few thin edges. Admission uses a random-walk score: walks from established agents measure how often they reach you, and isolated clusters score near zero. An attacker must buy or fake many long-lived links into real communities, paying in time, real services, and repeated interaction. Newcomers still get a haven: entry tasks slowly grow their edges. Basalt-hard to fake at scale, because the graph itself is the audit trail.
